summary: A 15-game slate defined by quarterback absences (Mayfield, Caleb Williams, Lamar Jackson likely, Daniels questionable) and a market that has already moved on several of them: BAL/ATL flipped six points and HOU/TEN's total fell two, killing a handful of analyst angles. The strongest theme is unders and team-total unders on bad or shorthanded offenses facing good defenses (MIA, NE, PHI, GB, MIN/NO, DEN/LAC, BUF/LA). Early, rough forecasts show wind at Lambeau (19 mph, gusts 27) and gusts of 30 with rain in Pittsburgh; they lean those unders the same way but none is built on weather, and Arizona's retractable roof should neutralize its windy drizzle.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: The 42.5 total and CIN -7 imply about 17.75 for Miami, yet it averages 11.5 points (32nd) and hasn't topped 13 in any game. The offense is 29th in EPA and 28th passing, and it just lost De'Von Achane to IR. Cincinnati brings a 7th-ranked pressure rate against a line the Bengals' report puts 27th at preventing sacks.
picks.risk: A defensive or special-teams score, or Bengals giveaways handing Miami short fields, can produce a cheap touchdown or two.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Both teams' reports agree: Las Vegas is 5th in net EPA with a +7.8 point differential, New England 16th at -3.0, yet the Raiders get more than a field goal. The Raiders' 2nd-ranked defense and 2nd-ranked pressure rate face an offense 21st in EPA with a -1.3 turnover margin, while New England's top corner Gonzalez is questionable.
picks.risk: The Raiders' 29th-ranked run game can't close games, and some of the 4-0 ATS run (+1.42 wins over expected) is luck that may regress.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: NE -3.5 with a 45.5 total implies about 24.5 for a Patriots offense averaging 16.3 (30th) that has cleared that number once, against the 29th-ranked defense. Now it faces the 2nd-ranked defense by EPA and the 2nd-best pressure rate with Hollins questionable and A.J. Brown on IR. Wind of 13 mph is not a factor.
picks.risk: Las Vegas's 29th-ranked red-zone defense turns field-goal drives into touchdowns.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Minnesota's offense is 27th in EPA, last in success rate and passes 5 points below expectation, and it has lost guard Donovan Jackson to IR with Jefferson questionable and Darrisaw in concussion protocol. Its defense is 1st in EPA, allowing 12.8 a game, and faces a Saints offense without Etienne. The Saints' report itself takes the under, and three of Minnesota's four games stayed under.
picks.risk: New Orleans' defense (26th in EPA, last against the run) pushed three of its four games over, and Saints turnovers (-1.3 a game) could hand Minnesota short fields.

picks.label: Shough sacks
picks.case: Minnesota leads the league in pressure rate (37.9%) and, per the report, sack rate (10.5%), and Shough turns 34.5% of pressures into sacks. He already took 12 sacks against weaker fronts. It's indoors, so nothing interferes with a straight pass-rush mismatch.
picks.risk: A quick-game plan built to get the ball out early, or a run-heavy script if the Saints lead, cuts dropbacks.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: These are near-identical teams: net EPA -0.094 vs -0.112, point differential -6.3 vs -7.0 a game, yet Houston, 0-4 ATS, lays more than a touchdown on the road. Houston's 30th-ranked run game can't bleed clock on a lead, and Tennessee covered as +7 and +11.5 underdogs. The move from 7 to 7.5 helps, and a total that fell to 37.5 makes a 7.5-point margin even harder to reach.
picks.risk: Tennessee's passing offense (25th, last in pass rate over expected) can't chase if it falls behind early.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Denver scores 18.5 a game (26th) and the Chargers 16.8 (29th), with the Chargers putting up 14, 14, 16 and 23. Los Angeles passes 9 points below expectation and now loses Slater, with Alt and two guards questionable. Three of Denver's four games went under, and it's indoors.
picks.risk: Denver's secondary is thin (Surtain doubtful, Moss with a rib issue), and the Chargers' turnovers could hand the Broncos short fields.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Green Bay scores 18.3 a game, has the league's worst rushing EPA and is missing center Monk (questionable) and tackle Bako-Bewele against the No. 2 pass defense and No. 3 pressure rate. Chicago, without Caleb Williams, leans run (23rd in pass rate over expected) and its last three games finished at 12, 34 and 35 points. The early forecast calls for 19 mph wind with 27 mph gusts, which would push the same way, but it's five days out.
picks.risk: Green Bay's 27th-ranked defense and leaky red zone let a backup quarterback score anyway, or the wind never materializes.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: The number matches Buffalo's game against the 32nd-ranked defense, but the Rams are 4th in EPA allowed and best against explosive and deep passes. Buffalo scored 24 and 26 against top-12 defenses, the Rams' offense is 15th in EPA at 21.3 points a game, and only one Rams game has cleared 54. Both reports agree.
picks.risk: Buffalo's 30th-ranked defense, missing corner Benford, lets Stafford pile up points, especially with Garrett on IR and Donald questionable on the other side.

picks.bet: BAL under its 153.5-a-game team rushing average
picks.label: Ravens rushing yards
picks.case: Atlanta has the league's best run defense (-0.307 EPA per rush, fewest explosive runs). Baltimore's rushing EPA has been negative two weeks running and guard Gwyn is on IR. Lamar Jackson is now reported unlikely to play, which removes a big piece of that 153.5 average; the line flipping from BAL -2.5 to ATL -3.5 says the market agrees.
picks.risk: A mobile backup or a run-heavy plan to protect him could pile up attempts, and Atlanta's -2 turnover margin could hand Baltimore extra possessions.

picks.label: Team total
picks.case: JAX -7 with a 42.5 total implies about 17.75 for an offense averaging 18.8, 28th in EPA and 30th in success rate, mostly with a healthier lineup. Goedert is doubtful, Jurgens is in concussion protocol, and Smith and Barkley are questionable. Jacksonville allows 13.3 points a game and opponents score touchdowns on 28.6% of red-zone trips.
picks.risk: If Smith and Barkley play and Jacksonville's deep-ball leaks show up, Philadelphia can get to 20; the red-zone number will also likely regress.

picks.label: Brissett passing yards
picks.case: Detroit allows a league-worst 350 yards a game to quarterbacks and ranks 30th in pass-defense EPA, and it's missing Ya-Sin (doubtful) and safety Harper (IR). The 54.5 total points to a shootout where Arizona trails, the script behind his 280-yard Week 3. The retractable roof should be closed against the drizzle and gusts.
picks.risk: With left tackle Paris Johnson on IR, pressure could cut his time, or Arizona could lean on its run game against Detroit's 29th-ranked run defense.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: All four reports that address the spread back Jacksonville: the net EPA gap is extreme (2nd vs 31st), Jacksonville leads the league at +1.5 turnovers a game, and Philadelphia is 0-4 ATS. Philadelphia's injuries hit its line and receivers, and its pass rush (31st in pressure rate) can't slow a 7th-ranked offense.
picks.risk: In London there's no real home field and 7 is a key number. Philadelphia's 4th-ranked special teams or a late score can land it exactly on 7 or backdoor it.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: Both passing offenses sit near the bottom (Colts 30th, Steelers 27th in pass EPA), and Indy, missing Pierce with Allen questionable, will lean on its league-best rushing offense. Pittsburgh's four games have averaged 41 combined points. An early forecast of 30 mph gusts and rain would help, but it's a hedge, not the case.
picks.risk: Pittsburgh's 27th-ranked deep defense gives up a couple of chunk plays, or Indy's -1.5 turnover margin hands the Steelers short fields.

picks.label: Game total
picks.case: All four Detroit games went over, averaging about 61.5 combined points, and Arizona's last two hit 66 and 60. Detroit's defense is 32nd in EPA and Arizona's pass defense 31st, while Detroit's passing offense ranks 4th. The 22 mph wind and drizzle forecast should be moot under a closed retractable roof.
picks.risk: The number is already high, and Arizona's clock control plus its 5th-ranked run defense could hold the game in the 40s.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: Tampa's defense is 5th in EPA and 3rd against the run, and all four of its losses came by seven or fewer. Dallas's defense is 31st and last against the pass, and only one of its four games was decided by more than nine. The line has moved from 9.5 to 8.5, losing a point, but still sits above the touchdown the reports' power gap suggests.
picks.risk: With Mayfield out, the league's worst passing offense may not score enough to stay within 8.5, and Winfield's absence opens the field for Dallas's 3rd-ranked passing attack.

picks.label: Spread
picks.case: San Francisco's net EPA (0.267, 1st) is more than double Seattle's (0.122), and its passing offense leads the league by a wide margin. Seattle's offense is 26th in rushing EPA and is missing its top two backs, which limits its ability to punish the 49ers' injuries. Getting points in a near pick'em with the better team is the edge.
picks.risk: Bosa (doubtful) and Sigle (out) weaken the defense, and the 49ers' numbers came largely against weak defenses, while Seattle's is 3rd in EPA. The reports also disagree on Seattle's quarterback, so check who starts.

picks.label: Love passing yards
picks.case: Chicago allows the third-fewest quarterback yards (210.3) and ranks 2nd in pass defense, and Love's average is propped up by 387- and 312-yard games in losing scripts. With Chicago's starter out and the Bears leaning on the run and clock, a long trailing script is less likely. Possible wind would help but isn't relied on.
picks.risk: If Green Bay falls behind early anyway, volume alone can push him past 260; corner Cam Lewis is also questionable for Chicago.

picks.label: Allen passing yards
picks.case: The Rams allow the fewest passing yards to quarterbacks (167.5) and the fewest explosive passes, and rank 1st against deep throws, where Allen's yardage comes from. He averaged 228.5 against the two top-12 defenses he has faced. It fits with the under on this game.
picks.risk: The Rams' 26th-ranked pressure rate, with Garrett on IR, gives Allen time, and a shootout with Stafford could inflate attempts.
